info.title: Triage Desk API
info.description: Stage 6 design for review. Paths are relative to the same-origin /api/v1 adapter. The ASP.NET Core service owns validation, authorization and writes. Examples use fictional records. Role claims and assignee identity always come from the server.

x-command-rules.accept: Owner/Reviewer; needsReview → ready. Priority and next step required. Optional assignment must name an active workspace member.
x-command-rules.requestInformation: Owner/Reviewer; needsReview → waitingForInformation. Require an active assignee and a question.
x-command-rules.setAside: Owner/Reviewer; needsReview → setAside. Require a reason.
x-command-rules.returnToReview: Owner/Reviewer; done or setAside → needsReview. Clear active assignment and reset inbox arrival time. Preserve prior values in history.
x-command-rules.reassign: Owner/Reviewer; ready, inProgress or waitingForInformation. Named assignee must be active. Only Ready may be unassigned.
x-command-rules.changePriority: Owner/Reviewer; ready or inProgress. Set a valid priority.
x-command-rules.changeSeverity: Owner/Reviewer; a severity value requires an applicable bug report. Null clears an existing value.
x-command-rules.editNextStep: Owner/Reviewer or the current assignee; ready or inProgress. Require a nonblank next step.
x-command-rules.complete: Current assignee; inProgress → done. Preserve the assignee for attribution. No external write.
x-command-rules.answer: Current assignee; waitingForInformation → needsReview. Preserve question and answer in history, clear assignment and reset inbox arrival time.
x-command-rules.acknowledgeSourceChange: Owner/Reviewer; a flag must exist. Clear a reviewed closure or reopening; transfer conflicts require confirmed identity resolution before clearing. Preserve the workflow status.

x-conventions.wire: UTF-8 JSON, camelCase, UTC ISO 8601 timestamps, UUID local identifiers. Serialize upstream numeric GitHub IDs as positive decimal strings. Limit request properties to the documented keys. Trim names, questions and reasons, and validate identifiers and enums before domain checks.
x-conventions.pages: One-based page, default pageSize 25, maximum 100. Return items, page, pageSize and total even on empty pages. Every list has a deterministic local ID tie-breaker. Workspace and member lists use name ascending; invitation and activity lists use newest first.
x-conventions.access: Resolve active membership, repository and issue inside workspaceId for every operation. Use 404 for a foreign or unknown resource and 403 for insufficient privilege on a visible resource. Validate an assignee against active membership in the same workspace.
x-conventions.writes: For claim and triage commands, authorize access, identify a prior committed command by workspace, issue, command ID and actor, and verify the stored input fingerprint before checking its old version. Matching retries return current authorized state without repeating effects. Reused command identity with different actor or input yields 409/command_id_reused. For a new command check current role, transition, expectedVersion and visibility; increment decisionVersion and append activity atomically. A confirmed no-op emits no duplicate activity. Ordinary upstream title changes do not increment decisionVersion.
x-conventions.errors: Use application/problem+json. Stable client-facing codes include validation_failed, unauthenticated, forbidden, csrf_failed, not_found, invitation_expired, already_claimed, stale_decision, invalid_transition, command_id_reused, open_run_exists, invalid_checkpoint, run_busy, rate_limited, upstream_error, service_unavailable and internal_error. Field mistakes use 400, valid commands incompatible with current state use 409. Unexpected 500 responses are generic and include a traceId.
x-conventions.compatibility: Ignore unknown response properties. Optional response fields and new routes may be added within v1. Breaking required fields, field meanings, closed enum sets or permission semantics require a new major path and a documented migration period. A public GitHub REST version is pinned independently.
x-conventions.visibility: All issue lists and metric drill-downs use connected, available sources. A direct local link to a retained issue may show private history and neutral source:null for an authorized member. Never include hidden imported text or labels in problem details or history.

fields.repository: id → githubRepositoryId (decimal text); full_name → fullName; html_url → webUrl. Verify visibility is public.
fields.issue: id → githubIssueId (decimal text); number, title, body and state map directly; labels[].name → labels; html_url → url; created_at and updated_at → sourceCreatedAt and sourceUpdatedAt. Set observedAt on a verified observation. Keep upstream assignees separate from internal ownership.
fields.pullRequests: Skip any issue-list row with a pull_request member. Use the issue number only within its verified repository.

x-github-integration.import: Initial public open issues, sorted by creation ascending, 100 per page. Incremental GitHub state=all, sort=updated, direction=asc, since=last successful watermark minus a small overlap. Store the cutoff at start, ignore later changes for this run and advance the watermark to the cutoff only on completion. Filter pull_request rows before upsert. An unseen closed record is skipped until observed open. Recheck public visibility and known sources during manual reconciliation; a missing list row alone is insufficient evidence. Bounded reconciliation and overlapping sweeps repair pagination drift on a changing upstream list.
x-github-integration.pagination: Follow validated same-host REST Link rel=next. Keep upstream cursors and leases on the server. A client submits only its local checkpoint. Match previously imported rows by stable external ID or verified alias.
x-github-integration.reconciliation: An explicit manual refresh may include bounded open-list rescans as well as per-record rechecks. Persist the reconciliation phase and position in the run cursor so changes in upstream pagination can be repaired. No schedule or background trigger is required.
x-github-integration.errors: Honor Retry-After and rate-limit reset. Distinguish quota-related 403/429 from access denial. Retry transient upstream errors with bounded backoff; never interpret timeout or failed pagination as confirmed removal. Re-verify canonical issue or repository and authorized redirect targets before applying visibility or transfer effects.

x-future-integrations.status: Deferred beyond MVP. No webhook receiver, SignalR hub or background delivery is an MVP operation.
x-future-integrations.webhooks: Future issues deliveries: verify raw-body HMAC-SHA256, reserve X-GitHub-Delivery durably and enqueue atomically before 202. Retry duplicate already-stored IDs safely. Route by verified public repository ID to independently authorized workspace connections. Canonically fetch the public issue; reuse the import transaction and fallback reconciliation. Retry processing durably and expose terminal failures.

signalr.delivery: Publish committed changes to a session-authorized workspace subscription. Revalidate active membership and revoke subscriptions on removal. An event is an invalidation hint: re-read authorized REST state, deduplicate by eventId and refetch on reconnect.
